title: In Deuteronomy 11 What Does It Mean To Love God With All Our Heart Soul And Might In A Practical Sense
paragraphs: Understanding Deuteronomy 11: Loving God with All Our Heart, Soul, and Might

Deuteronomy 11 is a powerful chapter in which Moses exhorts Israel to wholeheartedly love and obey the Lord as they prepare to enter the Promised Land. The command to love God “with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might” (Deuteronomy 6:5 ASV) is echoed throughout the book, and Deuteronomy 11 provides practical insights into what this love looks like in everyday life.
The Context of Deuteronomy 11

In this chapter, Moses reminds the Israelites of the Lord’s mighty acts and faithfulness during their journey from Egypt. He calls them to remember God’s commands, to teach them diligently to their children, and to write them on their hearts and homes. Loving God in this context is not merely an emotion, but a total commitment of one’s life to Him.

And it shall come to pass, if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love Jehovah your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul, that he will give the rain of your land in its season... - Deuteronomy 11:13-14 ASV
What Does It Mean to Love God “With All Your Heart, Soul, and Might”?

Heart: In the Old Testament, the “heart” refers to the seat of one’s thoughts, will, and emotions. To love God with all your heart means to set your deepest affections and desires upon Him, making Him the center of your decision-making and priorities (Proverbs 4:23 ASV).

Soul: The “soul” encompasses the whole being—your life, mind, and inner self. Loving God with all your soul means surrendering your entire life to Him, acknowledging that all you are belongs to Him (Psalm 103:1 ASV).

Might: “Might” refers to strength, resources, and energy. To love God with all your might means to devote your physical strength, abilities, and possessions to His service, using everything at your disposal for His glory (Colossians 3:23 ASV).
Practical Applications in Deuteronomy 11
Deuteronomy 11 offers several practical ways to express this wholehearted love for God:

Obeying God’s Commands: Love for God is demonstrated by obedience. Moses says, Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul... and ye shall teach them your children... - Deuteronomy 11:18-19 ASV Obedience flows from a heart that treasures God’s Word.

Teaching the Next Generation: Loving God involves passing on His truth to others, especially one’s children (Deuteronomy 11:19 ASV). This means making God’s commands part of daily life and conversation.
Remembering God’s Faithfulness: Moses urges the people to remember what God has done for them (Deuteronomy 11:2 ASV). Gratitude and remembrance fuel love and obedience.
Rejecting Idols and False Worship: True love for God means rejecting rivals and staying faithful to Him alone (Deuteronomy 11:16 ASV).
Serving God Wholeheartedly: Service is an outflow of love. We are called to serve God “with all your heart and with all your soul” (Deuteronomy 11:13 ASV).
Loving God in the New Testament
Jesus affirmed this as the greatest commandment:
And he said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the great and first commandment. - Matthew 22:37-38 ASV
This love is possible only through the transforming work of the Holy Spirit, who empowers believers to love and obey God from the heart (Romans 5:5 ASV).
Conclusion

To love God with all our heart, soul, and might is to make Him our highest affection, to surrender our whole lives, and to serve Him with all our strength. It is a call to wholehearted devotion, expressed through obedience, teaching, remembrance, and service. This love is both commanded and enabled by God, and remains the foundation of a life that pleases Him.
